reasoning: The filing prints two gross figures bearing on prior-year movement. The protocol's figure (underwriting years up to t-2) comes from the gross triangle: +42.907m, identical to the adopted figure. The note 19 line 'Change in prior year provisions' (gross 70,644) is wider in scope. The next line, 'Expected cost of current year claims' 119,661 (2023: 95,047), matches the 2024 (2023) first-year estimate in the triangle, 118,208 (94,853). So the prior-year line holds every underwriting year before 2024, including 2023, which is one of the two most recent years that criterion (c) excludes. The reinsurance side confirms this scope: the ceded-triangle steps for UW 2015-2023 sum to 55,509 against the note's reinsurance 'Change in prior year provisions' of 55,518. The two gross figures therefore reconcile rather than conflict: removing the 2023 step gives 41.097m against the adopted 42.907m, within tolerance. A literal reading that took the unadjusted 70.644 as the filing's figure would score an error (difference 27.737 > 2.145). But it would compare against a figure whose scope the protocol itself calls wrong, so I did not take it. Verdict: correct; the pipeline was right to override the model's note value.
